sets.name: Unit 01 Reading 1 야구를 하는데 춤도 춰?
sents: The batter steps up to the plate, and the pitcher stares at him.
You might think you’re watching a regular baseball game.
However, a song suddenly plays, and everyone on the field joins in a dance!
After that, the game continues as if nothing happened.
This unexpected scene is from a unique sport called Banana Ball.
Jesse Cole, a former baseball team manager, noticed that baseball fans were leaving games early out of boredom.
To make the game faster and more exciting, he founded the Savannah Bananas in 2016 and created Banana Ball.
Among its unique rules, the one that most distinguishes Banana Ball from traditional baseball is the two-hour time limit, which is about 40 minutes shorter than the average baseball game time.
Banana Ball offers fans special experiences through its distinct performances.
Players often dance, some of them wear stilts, and outfielders occasionally catch the ball with a 360-degree spin.
Furthermore, the Banana Nanas, a cheerleading squad made up of local women in their 60s, present a charming dance show during intermissions.
“We’re trying to make Banana Ball the greatest show in sports,” Cole said.
They seem to be succeeding, with millions of followers on TikTok.

sets.name: Unit 01 Reading 2 갓생에 지친 당신, ‘이것’ 모드 ON!
sents: Have you ever heard of the term goblin mode?
It refers to a state in which someone rejects social norms and expectations on purpose, choosing not to care about productivity or appearance.
Those in this state often spend their time on the couch, eating comfort food, and ignoring social pressure.
This laid-back trend involves deliberately rejecting productivity pressure to prioritize personal comfort and relaxation.
Goblin mode gained mainstream popularity during the COVID-19 pandemic when people grew tired of maintaining self-improvement habits during prolonged lockdowns.
This trend became so influential on social media that it was named Oxford Word of the Year in 2022.
Even in the post-pandemic era, there is still constant pressure to achieve more, look better, and be productive.
To deal with this, many people use goblin mode to reduce stress and feel better mentally.
They say no to society’s high standards and goals that are too hard to reach.
While goblin mode can be beneficial for mental health, it needs to be a temporary strategy.
Experts suggest that staying in this mode constantly can harm personal relationships, career development, and overall well-being by causing people to neglect their responsibilities.

sets.name: Unit 01 Reading 3 안녕, 외계인
sents: “Hello from the children of planet Earth” and “Annyeonghaseyo” are greetings from the Golden Record, a special time capsule sent into space!
The Golden Record is a record album made of gold-plated copper.
It was placed aboard NASA’s Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft, launched in 1977 to explore planets in our solar system.
The two spacecraft were programmed to continue their journey into interstellar space after completing their primary missions.
Recognizing the potential for these probes to be discovered by alien life, astronomer Carl Sagan had the idea to place a Golden Record on each one.
The purpose of this record is to serve as a message from Earth to any unknown alien civilizations that may encounter the probes.
The outside has instructions for use and a map indicating Earth’s location.
The inside includes 115 images showing aspects of life and science on Earth, such as the DNA structure and children playing.
It also features greetings in 55 languages and 90 minutes of music, including Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony.
These things reflect the diversity and complexity of life on Earth.
Since space is vast, the Golden Record may not be discovered for thousands of years.
Nevertheless, it shows humanity’s hope of finding other intelligent life and sharing our story.

sets.name: Unit 01 Reading 4 No Signal? Time to Reconnect!
sents: I’m a first-year high school student, and I spent my late elementary and middle school years during COVID-19.
Since I came back to in-person classes, I have found it hard to make new friends.
While I’m comfortable chatting online, I get nervous having face-to-face conversations.
What should I do?
Your experience is shared by many students of your generation.

Research reveals that the isolation brought about by COVID-19 has had a profound impact on young people’s social development, leaving many students struggling with social anxiety even after their return to in-person schooling.
But here’s the good news: our brains have amazing adaptability, especially at your age.
Start with small steps to rebuild your confidence.
Try simple actions like saying “hello” to classmates.
Joining school clubs is another great option because shared activities naturally reduce social pressure.
Most importantly, however, it should be remembered that your peers are likely to feel the same way, though they may not overtly express it.
Be patient with yourself as your social confidence grows with practice!

sets.name: Unit 02 Reading 1 얌전히 나가면 봐줄게
sents: It goes without saying that freedom is a basic human right.
But does that right extend to prisoners as well?
Surprisingly, in Germany, it is not illegal to escape from prison as long as it’s done without any crimes being committed.
This legal stance traces back to 1871 when the German Criminal Code (Strafgesetzbuch) was enacted.
The code imposed imprisonment for helping or inducing a prisoner to escape.
But it did not include punishment for prisoners who escaped on their own.
This decision reflects the legal philosophy that seeking freedom is a natural human desire—one that should not, in itself, be treated as a criminal offense.
This historical legal principle continues to apply today.
While the escape itself is not punishable, inmates are liable for any illegal acts committed during their escapes, such as damaging prison property or bribing guards.
However, some legal experts have presented opposing views.
They warn that allowing unpunished prison escapes weakens the enforcement of the criminal justice system and the authority of the law.

sets.name: Unit 02 Reading 2 척하면 척
sents: As you pass by a busy construction site, you hear one of the workers yell, “Brick!”
Is the worker identifying an object, making a request, shouting a warning, or doing something else altogether?
Despite knowing the definition of the word brick, it is impossible for you to determine the specific contextual meaning without additional information.
The Austrian philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein attempted to explain this phenomenon through the concept of language games.
He argued that different communication activities—such as making a joke—are types of language games that have a distinct set of rules based on the shared understanding of the players.
For example, you would certainly be confused if someone randomly said to you, “Across the street.”
However, if you had just asked for directions to the nearest subway station, the response would make perfect sense.
Wittgenstein’s theory also shows miscommunications can happen when people apply different language games to identical situations.
Take the case of one office worker notifying another about an upcoming meeting and receiving the response, “Oh great, another meeting.”

The first worker, looking forward to the meeting, might interpret the remark literally, but the second, annoyed by the number of meetings lately, may have intended to express displeasure through sarcasm.
Since they are each playing a different language game, they cannot truly understand each other.

sets.name: Unit 02 Reading 3 일단 싸게 부르고 보자!
sents: Alice heads to the electronics store, planning to spend about $1,500 on a new computer.
The seller suggests a nice one for $1,300.
However, as soon as she agrees to buy that one, he mentions that the software she needs costs extra.
As a result, the final price jumps to $1,700.
Despite going over her budget, she buys that computer.
This is a classic example of the lowball technique.
The lowball technique is a strategy where salespeople first present a low, reasonable price and then raise it after customers decide to buy.
Although the origin of the term lowball is unclear, it is similar to a pitcher’s strategy in baseball, throwing low balls intentionally to deceive batters and achieve outs.
Why do we often accept such unfair deals?
This occurs because several psychological factors affect our decision-making process.
We instinctively worry about leaving a negative impression on others by reversing the first decision, even when conditions have become worse.
Moreover, we tend to avoid wasting the time and effort already invested in making the purchase decision.

sets.name: Unit 02 Reading 4 Sand Fades, Stone Stays
sents: Two lifelong friends, Jordan and Sam, were journeying across a vast desert.
Under the scorching sun, they walked on until they had a bitter argument about which path to take.
The argument escalated when Jordan spoke harshly.
After that, they walked at a distance from each other.
Feeling hurt, Sam knelt down and wrote in the sand.
“Today, my best friend’s words stayed with me longer than they should have.”
They continued their journey in silence until they discovered an oasis.
While resting there, Sam’s foot slipped on the wet rocks, and he was about to drown.
Without hesitation, Jordan dove in and saved his friend’s life.
After he recovered, Sam carved in a nearby rock, “Today, my best friend saved my life with his bravery.”
Puzzled by this, Jordan asked, “When I upset you, you wrote in the sand, but now you carve in stone.
What is the difference?”
Sam replied with a gentle smile, “When someone hurts us, we should write it in sand, so the winds of forgiveness can easily erase it.
But when someone shows us kindness, we must engrave it in stone, where no wind can ever erase it.”

sets.name: Unit 03 Reading 1 편한데 재미있기까지?
sents: Have you ever thought that taking an escalator felt like being on a fun ride?
If so, that’s not surprising.
The first functional escalator debuted as a thrilling ride at Coney Island, New York, where over 75,000 visitors excitedly tried it out!
Called the “Inclined Elevator,” it was constructed in 1896 by American engineer Jesse Reno.
It smoothly transported passengers up and down a slope.
Following this success, more escalators appeared in various locations.
In 1900, Charles Seeberger, an American inventor, introduced the term escalator, combining the Latin word scala, meaning “steps,” with the “elevator.”
He partnered with the Otis Elevator Company to launch escalators as an innovative form of transportation.
Their escalators were so successful that they were awarded the Grand Prize at the Paris Exposition!
Since then, escalators have evolved significantly, making it easier to move between floors while prioritizing safety and efficiency in modern designs.
Consequently, they have become a vital component of our everyday life!

sets.name: Unit 03 Reading 2 바닷속 탄소 감옥, 그 끈적한 비밀은?
sents: Seaweed has long been a common ingredient in cuisines around the world.
Rich in nutrients, foods made with seaweed are widely considered beneficial to human health.
But did you know that seaweed may benefit not only human health, but also the health of our planet?
Classified as brown algae, this ocean-living organism has recently gained attention for its ability to fight climate change.
According to research conducted by the Max Planck Institute, some species of brown algae can absorb up to 550 million tons of carbon from seawater each year.
More importantly, this captured carbon does not easily reenter the natural carbon cycle.
But how does this happen?
Like plants, brown algae obtain energy for growth by absorbing carbon and turning it into sugar through photosynthesis.
During this process, they release excess sugar back into the water.
In one type of brown algae called bladderwrack, around half of this sugar becomes a hard and sticky substance that fish and other organisms cannot eat.
This substance then sinks to the ocean floor, where it can remain for hundreds or thousands of years.
By locking away carbon, it contributes to reducing the amount of greenhouse gases that harm our planet.

sets.name: Unit 03 Reading 3 잘 모르겠지만, 그때가 그리워요
sents: In 2024, K-pop group Riize released “Love 119,” a song that takes people back to the good old days of 2005—but the group’s youngest member was born in 2004!
How can they sing about missing a time when they were just babies?
And why do so many young listeners of this song become nostalgic for that time in the past, even though some weren’t even born yet?
This emotional longing for an era that we never experienced personally is called “anemoia.”
It combines the Greek words anemos (wind) and noia (mind), capturing the idea of a mind blown by winds from the past.
This phenomenon is often triggered by viewing vintage films and photographs or listening to retro songs.
These forms of media give us an idealized representation of what life was like for the generations before us.
Faced with this curated content, we tend to believe that everything was easier back then, especially if we aren’t content with the present.
The entertainment industry uses this cognitive bias to enhance its commercial appeal.
Film directors and music producers look to the past to create romanticized versions of different times in history.
This trend leaves members of Generation Z aching for something that they never really lost.

sets.name: Unit 03 Reading 4 Freeze! Who Goes First?
sents: Which would freeze faster, something hot or something cold?
It seems straightforward.
But the answer may surprise you.
Hot water may freeze in less time than cold water!
This strange phenomenon was observed by a Tanzanian man named Erasto Mpemba in the 1960s, and it is now known as the Mpemba effect.
But how could this be possible?
One possible explanation is that hot water evaporates more quickly, reducing the total amount of water that needs to freeze.
Less water means a shorter freezing time.
In addition, hot water tends to circulate more actively due to convection, which helps it cool evenly throughout.
Another factor is that hot water can heat the bottom of the container and melt any frost underneath.
This lets the container sit more closely on the cold freezer surface, so heat can move out more quickly.
Cold water, on the other hand, may form a thin layer of ice on the surface early on, acting as insulation and slowing down further cooling.
However, the validity of the Mpemba effect is still debated among scientists.
Some critics argue that the water’s freezing rate depends on the purity of the water and the properties of the container that holds the water.

sets.name: Unit 04 Reading 1 이열치열 대신 이음치음
sents: Beep beep!
Car horns honk.
Blah blah blah.
Loud chatter fills the air.
The city is full of noise, and you find it all so annoying!
But once you slip on your earphones, the noise fades away, leaving you in a world of peaceful silence.
This is possible due to noise-canceling technology.
Earphones incorporating this technology reduce outside sounds through the process of destructive interference.
There are two sound waves involved in this process.
One comes from the noise around you, and the other is from the noise-canceling earphones.
The earphones use microphones to detect external sounds and then produce a new wave called anti-noise with the exact opposite pattern of the detected sound wave.
When these two opposite waves meet, they cancel out each other, resulting in silence.
It’s like two people are pushing on opposite sides of a door with equal force—nothing happens because they balance each other.
This canceling-out effect of destructive interference allows you to enjoy the silence even in noisy surroundings!

sets.name: Unit 04 Reading 2 돌잔치 때 휴대폰 잡은 아이들
sents: Toddlers chat with smart voice assistants, and students do homework with AI chatbots.
Welcome to the world of Generation Alpha, the first generation born entirely in the 21st century!
Generation Alpha refers to those born between 2010 and approximately 2025.
Their most distinctive characteristic compared to other generations is that they are true “digital natives.”
Since they have grown up with digital technology from birth, Generation Alpha has superior access to and proficiency with digital devices and technologies like virtual assistants and AI.
Therefore, they are able to navigate digital environments with ease from a very young age.
This digital fluency can give them broad access to diverse information.
Instead of only being exposed to traditional media sources like newspapers and TV news, they communicate with digital communities and consume informative short-form content.
Through them, they can naturally develop clear opinions about what is going on in the world.

By engaging with a wide range of viewpoints from a young age, members of Generation Alpha more openly talk about their views and cases of unfairness and gladly share them on social media to raise awareness and encourage action.
As this generation grows older, their digital fluency and social awareness will likely help create important social change.

sets.name: Unit 04 Reading 3 킁킁, 글씨 냄새 맡는 중입니다만?
sents: Read the following sentence: She wrapped herself in a warm blanket and took a sip of hot chocolate.
Did you feel the thickness of the blanket and smell the rich aroma of the hot chocolate while you read it?
Most likely you could.

This phenomenon is the result of a fascinating aspect of cognitive neuroscience: when we read about experiences, our brains can trigger neural pathways as if we were actually experiencing those sensations.
Researchers have discovered that words associated with strong sensations activate sensory areas just as our senses do.
For instance, the word chocolate stimulates the primary olfactory cortex and the gustatory cortex, the regions of the brain responsible for processing smell and taste.
What’s interesting is that activating those cortexes does more than simply enable us to recall specific sensations.
It actually helps us experience the characters’ situations and emotions, allowing us to develop greater empathy for them.
This response is rooted in the brain’s embodied cognition, the idea that our thinking processes involve both sensory and emotional experiences.
This neural activation highlights the importance of reading in our lives.
By engaging multiple sensory systems, it offers us a kind of second life, broadening our understanding of the world!

sets.name: Unit 04 Reading 4 Your Seat Is on the Stage
sents: Natasha, Pierre & the Great Comet of 1812 is a musical inspired by Leo Tolstoy’s War and Peace.
This production offers you the best immersive theater experience, where every detail enhances your journey into the heart of Tolstoy’s world!
Dive into the magic of immersive theater, where you’re not just a spectator but also a participant.
This unique form of performance art allows you to experience life in 19th-century Russia, which was profoundly shaped by war and love.
One way this immersion is achieved is through the transformation of physical space.
For example, the theater may be decorated to match the setting of a 19th-century Russian tearoom.
Interestingly, this often applies to the seating area as well.
Details such as background sounds and scents may be included for a richer experience.
But the real fun lies in the interaction!
In immersive theater, actors often move through the audience, and audience members may find themselves engaging in lively dialogue.
This can influence the choices of characters in the play, and it can even completely change the ending!
This type of engagement allows for a unique experience, as no two performances are the same.
With your choices shaping the story, be ready to play your part.
There is always a seat waiting for you!

sets.name: Unit 05 Reading 1 내 것만 아니면 되는 거죠?
sents: Two lawyers named Chad and Robin entered a downtown diner.
After settling at a table, they proceeded to order drinks.
“Nothing to eat?” the server asked.
Chad and Robin shook their heads.
As she left to get the beverages, they opened their briefcases and took out big, homemade sandwiches —clearly not from the diner.
They started eating casually, as if this was something they did all the time.
However, this quickly attracted the attention of the diner’s owner, Mr. Monroe, who didn’t like people bringing their own food into his restaurant.
In fact, it was against the rules!
He marched over to the table and said, “Hey guys, you can’t eat your own sandwiches in here!”
Chad and Robin smiled slyly at each other before responding, “OK.”
They then shrugged and exchanged sandwiches.
Just then, a man at the next table, who had been quietly observing them, suddenly stood up.
Smiling, he said, “Nice try, but your little exchange doesn’t change the rules” and then showed his police badge.

sets.name: Unit 05 Reading 2 마음이 안 가면 눈도 없어요
sents: If eyes are the windows to one’s soul, what might it mean when an artist deliberately chooses not to depict them?
The Italian painter Amedeo Modigliani is renowned for this distinctive choice.
In many of his portraits, the subject’s eyes remain uncolored, which makes them appear blank.
This was not just about style, but rather a meaningful personal decision.
Some who have studied Modigliani’s work believe that he would only paint the eyes of subjects he felt emotionally connected to.
These included his partner Jeanne Hébuterne, close friends, and even young street children whom he felt sympathy for.
While the emotional connection to his subjects appears to be one factor in Modigliani’s portrayal of eyes, artistic influences also played a significant role.
In the early 1900s, the renowned sculptor Constantin Brancusi introduced Modigliani to African sculpture, which featured simplified, abstract faces.
Inspired by these works, Modigliani began creating portraits with blank eyes.
He removed unnecessary details, allowing viewers to focus on the essence of the subject.

sets.name: Unit 05 Reading 3 으악! 훅 들어오시면 곤란해요!
sents: We’ve all been there: that awkward moment when a distant, unfamiliar relative pulls us in for a tight hug.
In this situation, do you feel warm and safe, or does your whole body tense up?
What determines these different responses to a sudden touch?
It’s not just your personality or preference.
It’s what happens in your brain!
When we have a positive response to physical contact, it happens because our brain releases oxytocin, called the “trust hormone.”
Increased oxytocin levels create feelings of security and help us to develop emotional connections.
But what about uncomfortable physical contact like unwanted hugs?
That’s when your brain hits the panic button.
It releases large amounts of cortisol, the “stress hormone.”
This heightened state causes increased anxiety and an overwhelming urge to escape the situation.
You also experience physical symptoms such as increased heart rate, sweating, and muscle tension.
These responses evolved to help early humans survive immediate physical threats, such as predators.
Today, this serves as our body’s natural warning system, helping us avoid threatening situations.

sets.name: Unit 05 Reading 4 Open Your Mouth, Open Your World
sents: Recent rapid technological advancements seem to be raising concerns that they could pose threats to humanity.
But there is also a bright side to tech innovation.
Through innovative assistive software, numerous individuals with disabilities are acquiring unprecedented autonomy!
Dragon NaturallySpeaking is one such software that allows users to convert their spoken words into text and control some computer functions through voice commands.
This can be especially helpful for students with physical disabilities or vision impairments who have difficulty using a keyboard or a mouse.
In addition, it adapts to each person’s unique manner of speaking, so that it can understand people with speech impediments as well.
Another program making a positive impact for the disabled is Otter.ai, which provides real-time transcription.
When users join a video meeting, it automatically records the content and identifies the speaker, allowing individuals with hearing impairments to independently participate in online classes.
Ultimately, whether a technology helps or hurts us depends on how it’s used.
When advancements focus on ethical goals, they can enhance accessibility and contribute to a more inclusive society.

sets.name: Unit 06 Reading 1 사막을 빛내는 거대한 도시
sents: NEOM, despite facing delays and scale reductions, was once widely regarded as the future of urban living.
NEOM is a large-scale urban development project whose name combines neo (new) and the Arabic word mustaqbal (future).
As a key part of Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030, it was planned to be a sizable, modern, sustainable city that protects the natural environment.
NEOM’s most notable feature was supposed to be The Line.
This is one of the planned cities within NEOM, and it was designed to take the form of an enormous linear structure that measures 170 kilometers in length and 500 meters in height.
Its exterior was to be covered with mirrors that reflect the surrounding environment, making it blend harmoniously with nature.
Additionally, important places such as healthcare centers and grocery stores were to use automated, smart technologies and be located within a five-minute walk of people’s homes.
Although about nine million people were expected to live in The Line, there were to be no cars or roads.
Instead, a fast train system that runs on 100 percent clean energy was to be built underground, helping people to move throughout The Line.
This would have made life more convenient for residents while contributing to the goal of zero carbon emissions.

sets.name: Unit 06 Reading 2 질병을 막아주는 신비한 부리
sents: In the 14th century, a deadly epidemic known as the Black Death swept across Europe, claiming nearly a third of the continent’s population.
But this plague never truly disappeared; it reappeared in the 17th century, prompting the introduction of plague doctors.
Without understanding the plague’s true cause, these doctors relied on unusual methods to protect themselves while treating the infected.
Their strange outfit was one example.
We now know the plague was caused by a type of bacteria spread by flea bites and contact with infected people.
Back then, however, people believed the cause was poisoned air.

Based on this poor medical knowledge, a French physician named Charles de Lorme devised an outfit consisting of a thick leather coat, gloves, and a mask to prevent the skin from coming into contact with contaminated air.
The defining feature was the long beak of the mask, which made doctors look like birds!
Doctors filled the beak with strong-scented herbs, convinced that smelling these would keep them safe.
While the coat and gloves offered limited protection, the mask was almost useless.
Nose holes poked into the beak to let the wearers breathe allowed germs to enter, causing them to be infected!

sets.name: Unit 06 Reading 3 간지럼은 남로내불?!
sents: Out of nowhere, a hand sneaks up under your armpit.
Instantly, uncontrollable laughter erupts, as if that hidden “laugh spot” had been waiting for the perfect tickle!
But have you ever tried to tickle yourself?
Most will find it impossible, and the reason lies in how the brain processes touch.
When someone else tickles us, the unpredictability of the touch plays a key role.
Brain scans of people being tickled show activation in brain areas related to touch, emotions, and pleasure.
These activated regions process the tickling sensation and lead to laughter.
On the other hand, in the case of self-tickling, the cerebellum —the part of the brain responsible for body and muscle control— becomes active.
The cerebellum is highly aware of our bodily movements, allowing us to expect that we are about to tickle ourselves.
As a result, it stops the brain areas responsible for touch and pleasure from activating.

This mechanism helps the brain distinguish between sensations caused by our own actions and those coming from the outside world, ensuring we stay more sensitive to unexpected touches that might require our attention.

sets.name: Unit 06 Reading 4 Keep Your Hands Off Mickey!
sents: Everyone loves Mickey Mouse.
And so do his creators at Disney.
The company valued him so much that it strived to make a law to protect him!
This is known as the Mickey Mouse Protection Act.
When this character first appeared in the 1928 film Steamboat Willie, its original copyright was valid for 56 years.
This meant Disney had exclusive rights to profit from the use of Mickey Mouse until 1984.
However, in the 1970s, Disney lobbied Congress to extend this protection.
Their efforts paid off in 1976 when they successfully ensured their ownership for an additional 19 years.
Even more lobbying followed in the 1990s, resulting in the passage of the Mickey Mouse Protection Act in 1998.
This guaranteed Disney’s rights to Mickey Mouse until the end of 2023.
In 2024, the original version of the character from Steamboat Willie entered the public domain, making it free for anyone to use without permission.

While this act has been controversial, as many criticized it for extending copyrights only to benefit large corporations like Disney, some people view it as highlighting the importance of protecting intellectual property within the entertainment industry.

sets.name: Unit 07 Reading 1 어른이 되기 싫은 피터 팬들
sents: From Bob Dylan to BLACKPINK, many artists across generations have released songs titled “Forever Young.”
They seem to echo the wishes of many “Peter Pans” in our society!
Just like the fictional character Peter Pan, adulthood still feels out of reach for them.
Individuals suffering from Peter Pan Syndrome generally exhibit immature behavior.
They tend to rely heavily on family members to cope with the challenges of everyday life.
They are reluctant to embrace adult responsibilities, which makes it challenging to navigate the demands of adult life.
Although the exact causes of this reluctance are not fully understood, many experts believe it results from early life experiences.
Especially, when parents are overly protective during their children’s teenage years, it can limit adolescents’ opportunities to make important decisions and face the consequences of their mistakes.
However, we must understand Peter Pan Syndrome beyond early home life and consider its societal roots.
Economic challenges, such as rising living costs and job instability, have made being an adult much harder, causing prolonged dependence on parents.

sets.name: Unit 07 Reading 2 흑역사를 사랑하라...?
sents: Amor fati, a Latin phrase meaning “love of fate,” is a weighty philosophical concept explored by Friedrich Nietzsche.
He urged us not merely to accept our lives but to appreciate every twist and turn with open arms.
In a world where we often feel lost in difficult situations, Nietzsche’s call might seem radical.
He, however, believed that to truly live, one must see everything as both necessary and beautiful, as if it were part of a cosmic plan.
In practice, this means we should celebrate our failures as often as our successes.
Instead of being paralyzed by the fear of making mistakes, we can learn to view every misstep as a stepping stone toward personal growth.
This mindset not only fosters resilience but also cultivates a deeper appreciation for the journey of life itself!

sets.name: Unit 07 Reading 3 파멸로 이끄는 새 집
sents: As the sun sets, hermit crabs come out of their burrows to search for food.
But instead of natural shells, some of them have something shocking on their backs—a bright blue plastic container.
What’s going on?
Hermit crabs are marine creatures found in various coastal environments.
In the wild, they typically protect their soft bodies with empty snail shells.
This serves as an effective defense mechanism against predators, thereby keeping them safe.
However, as millions of tons of plastic waste enter the oceans each year, hermit crabs are increasingly using plastic containers instead of natural shells.
This is because they are attracted to oleamide, a chemical found in some plastics.
When crabs absorb harmful chemical compounds from plastics into their bodies, they undergo behavioral changes that reduce their food-foraging ability.
In addition, using brightly colored plastic containers as shells makes them more visible to predators.
This lowers their chances of survival in the wild.

sets.name: Unit 07 Reading 4 Am I Competing with Myself?
sents: Imagine you own a café known for its delicious hot chocolate.
It has been your bestseller for years.
Still, you’re eager to boost your sales and start thinking of a new menu item.
One day, you get a great idea: to launch a brand-new sweet milk tea at an affordable price.
But you hesitate to introduce the new drink because you are worried that customers might stop buying the hot chocolate.
This is known as the cannibalization dilemma.
Cannibalization describes a situation in which a company’s new product competes with an existing one.
On the bright side, it can drive innovation and increase a company’s overall market share by expanding product lines to meet changing consumer preferences.
On the other hand, the company risks losing customers and sales of the existing product.
Many companies face this tension between innovating and protecting existing business.
A well-known example can be found in Apple’s product strategy.
When Apple introduced the iPhone, it included music features that could replace a separate music player like the iPod.
Still, Apple’s co-founder Steve Jobs argued that a company should not be afraid of “cannibalizing” itself, because if it doesn’t, someone else will.
Even if the new product threatened an older bestseller, Apple pushed forward, which led to one of the most significant sales increases in the company’s history.
Apple’s success shows that embracing cannibalization can sometimes open the door to groundbreaking innovation.

sets.name: Unit 08 Reading 1 손 못 드는 너한테 알려주고 싶어
sents: In class, there are always some students who confidently raise their hands while others hesitate.
The secret of their confidence lies in self-efficacy, a concept introduced by Canadian-American psychologist Albert Bandura.
It refers to people’s belief in their ability to accomplish specific tasks, and it influences how students approach challenges.
According to Bandura, self-efficacy stems from four sources.
First, personal experiences play a crucial role.
For example, successfully solving difficult math problems by oneself boosts confidence for similar tasks.
Second, observing others’ successes also strengthens self-efficacy.
Watching a friend master a skill can make you feel that you can succeed as well.
Third, verbal encouragement from teachers or parents can lead to greater faith in one’s abilities.
Finally, psychological states are important.
Reducing feelings of stress or anxiety helps one to feel more capable.

Students can develop self-efficacy by setting small, achievable goals to experience success, seeking constructive feedback from teachers and parents, and implementing effective stress management techniques.
This will help them develop confidence, ultimately leading to better academic performance and personal growth.

sets.name: Unit 08 Reading 2 덕질도 육각형 시대
sents: K-pop fans are among the most passionate in the world.
They line up all night at pop-up stores for exclusive fan goods or purchase dozens of albums to increase their chances of winning a raffle to meet their idols.
Their enthusiasm is so intense that they are not satisfied with simply consuming existing content from major K-pop entertainment agencies.
In the fandustry, fans are also producers, creators, and leaders.
The term fandustry, which combines fan and industry, refers to a rapidly growing industry with an estimated market size of $600 million.
It represents a truly fan-driven industry where both producers and consumers are fans themselves.
For example, some fans create their own goods, such as dolls, keychains, and custom art, which often sell out instantly to eager fans.
Other enthusiastic fans raise money through crowdfunding to display advertisements on subway stations and downtown billboards to celebrate stars’ birthdays or other milestones.
They even rent out entire cafes to host “birthday cafes”, fan events dedicated to celebrating stars’ birthdays.

sets.name: Unit 08 Reading 3 내 안의 야수를 깨워라
sents: You’re halfway through your workout, your muscles are screaming for mercy, and you are almost exhausted.
But then, something kicks in, and you suddenly feel unstoppable.
It feels like you’re ready to lift more weight or sprint another 100 meters.
Welcome to “beast mode!”
Beast mode is a state in which a person releases overwhelming energy and passion to reach a higher level of performance.
The expression was popularized by former National Football League (NFL) superstar Marshawn Lynch.
Once he grabbed the ball and started running, no one could stop him.
It was as if he transformed into a beast.
His explosive performances became known as beast mode.
When you enter beast mode, adrenaline surges through the body—an adrenaline rush!
It significantly boosts the function of muscles and organs like the heart and lungs, while increasing alertness.
This enhanced state improves muscle endurance, sharpens reflexes, and increases oxygen efficiency, elevating performance to meet extreme physical demands.
Of course, it is difficult to reach beast mode.
But once the inner beast is unleashed, you can push yourself beyond your limits!

sets.name: Unit 08 Reading 4 Serving Up Equality
sents: As Billie Jean King, a female tennis star, stepped onto the court, 90 million people watched.
On the opposite side stood Bobby Riggs, former men’s tennis No.1.
With a deep breath, she served; this moment marked a milestone for women’s sports!
King was born in Long Beach, California, in 1943.
As an exceptional athlete, she began playing tennis at the age of 11.
In 1961, Billie Jean King won her first Wimbledon Women’s Doubles Championship, partnering with Karen Hantze.
They became the youngest team to win the Wimbledon doubles title at that time.
From then on, she continued to achieve great success, collecting 39 Grand Slam titles throughout her career.
Among her many achievements, the most influential was her victory against Bobby Riggs in 1973.
It not only led to increased women’s participation in sports but also strengthened her ongoing campaign for equal prize money between men and women.
In addition to her impact on the court, she actively promoted women’s rights in sports.
She established the Women’s Tennis Association and the Women’s Sports Foundation.
In recognition of her contributions, the women’s international team tennis competition, formerly known as the Fed Cup, was renamed the Billie Jean King Cup in 2020.

sets.name: Unit 09 Reading 1 할머니! 이 옷 어디서 난 거야?
sents: If you need an idea for a trendy outfit, you might want to check your grandmother’s closet.
One of the latest fashion trends is based on her style.
The unique fashion trend called “Grandmillennial” or Granny Chic has recently captured the hearts of young people.
It features cozy fabrics and vintage clothing.
The comfortable nature of oversized sweaters appeals to those looking for relief from modern life’s stress.
While you may buy new clothes for Granny Chic, you can also choose secondhand clothes, which is a sustainable way to be stylish!
Granny Chic allows for personal expression through creative combinations of vintage pieces that are traditionally overlooked by younger generations.
You can mix and match oversized jewelry, like brooches or ear clips, with bright floral prints to express your individuality.
This style proves that sometimes, the best fashion inspiration comes from the past.

sets.name: Unit 09 Reading 2 문이 닫혔다, 천재가 열었다
sents: One night in 1937, Marian Anderson, a talented singer who transformed the landscape of opera, gave a performance at McCarter Theatre, New Jersey.
The whole audience applauded her enthusiastically!
Despite her outstanding performance, however, she was turned away by a hotel in the area.
The only reason was that she was Black.
Fortunately, a fan who had been at the show heard this and suggested that she stay at his nearby home.
Believe it or not, this generous fan was the great physicist, Albert Einstein!
This was the start of their unique friendship.
They shared a strong interest in music.
Einstein loved music so much that he once said, “If I were not a physicist, I would probably be a musician.”
But that wasn’t the only thing they had in common.
They both raised their voices against racism.
Anderson was renowned for her role in the civil rights movement, while Einstein urged white Americans to confront the problem of racism, calling it “a disease of white people.”
From that special night, they stayed close friends, exemplifying a profound bond that went beyond race!

sets.name: Unit 09 Reading 3 흘렸으면 치우셔야죠!
sents: “No way!” you shout loudly as you crouch to pick up your phone from under the bed.
There’s so much dust down there!
Could it be because of all the fine dust in the air outside?
Actually, much of the dust under your bed is made up of tiny pieces of your skin!
According to research by Dutch biologist Johanna van Bronswijk, up to 50 percent of household dust comes from the human body.
In fact, you shed about 500 million skin cells each day.
Some of them find their way under the bed.
Over time, they mix with other dust particles from various sources like pollen and clothes.
The problem is that this buildup of dust not only negatively affects your breathing, but it also allows unwanted bugs to hide.
That’s why it’s important to sweep under your bed regularly.
So what are you waiting for?
Get a broom and start cleaning!

sets.name: Unit 09 Reading 4 Boss, This Is Not a Waste of Time!
sents: Some office workers are gathered in the lounge, laughing over a joke when their boss walks in, frowning at the employees.
But actually, he shouldn’t be too concerned.
According to researchers at MIT’s Human Dynamics Lab, social interactions like this can benefit the company, increasing productivity among workers!
This is due to the water cooler effect, which is named after the machine that dispenses drinking water.
Employees typically gather around it and have casual conversations on subjects unrelated to work, such as entertainment or sports.
The effect can occur around other shared devices, such as a coffee machine or printer.
Those with common interests can form bonds while chatting.
And as they become more comfortable with one another, it becomes more natural to talk about the challenges they face at work!
This can lead to more efficient problem solving and even collaboration on projects.
Recently, with the rise of remote work, the water cooler is being replaced by online platforms where people can engage in casual conversations through instant messaging.
They’re not simply wasting their time; they’re strengthening relationships through mutual understanding.

sets.name: Unit 10 Reading 1 상심도 병원비가 나옵니다
sents: When we go through tough times, we often say we are heartbroken.
But having a broken heart is more than just an expression.
As it turns out, intense sadness or stress can actually affect the human heart negatively, resulting in a real condition called broken-heart syndrome.
When faced with emotional trauma, our body responds by releasing a stress hormone called adrenaline.
The release of adrenaline causes the small arteries that carry blood to the heart to get tighter, leading to a short-term drop in blood flow.
The adrenaline may even attach directly to the heart cells, which can stop the heart from beating normally.
In extreme cases, the heart temporarily changes shape, with part of it increasing in size and becoming less effective at pumping blood.
The end result is an experience similar to that of a heart attack, including chest pain, dizziness, and breathing difficulty.
But unlike with a heart attack, patients are mostly safe from permanent heart damage.
Therefore, they tend to make a full recovery within weeks or even a few days.

sets.name: Unit 10 Reading 2 내 이름이 적힌 콜라가 있다?
sents: On a hot summer day, you rush into a convenience store and head straight to the drinks section.
There, you see a drink with your name on it!
Would you buy it?
You probably would.
This emotional appeal is a psychological strategy that Coca-Cola wisely used in its product marketing.
In 2011, the Coca-Cola branch in Australia was experiencing decreasing sales.
The company launched the “Share a Coke” campaign to address this.
For the campaign, 150 of the most common names in the nation, such as David and Lucy, were printed on bottles.
Remarkably, sales of Coca-Cola increased by 4 percent, leading to the campaign’s expansion to over 70 other countries.
Some nations added creative twists by using job titles like “teacher” or “police officer” as well as terms of affection like “friend,” while keeping the original concept.
The key to the success of the “Share a Coke” campaign lies in personalization.
Seeing their own names on the bottles created a strong connection with the product, making the consumers’ purchases feel special.
It was also common for buyers to pick bottles with particular names so that they could present them as gifts to family and friends.

sets.name: Unit 10 Reading 3 하늘로 솟구치는 온천
sents: Anyone planning a trip to New Zealand should visit Te Puia, a natural wonderland located on the North Island.
About the size of 70 football fields, it is sure to amaze you!
Meaning “the hot spring” in Maori, Te Puia is famous for its geysers—natural vents that regularly erupt, shooting steam and water into the air.
It is home to the Pohutu Geyser, the largest active geyser in the Southern Hemisphere.
Erupting up to 20 times a day, it produces columns of steam and water to a maximum of 30 meters in height.
Te Puia offers more than natural wonders.
This site also holds great cultural significance for the Maori people, who have called it home for centuries.
To share their rich history, the Maori have established a cultural center at the site.
Here, visitors can observe traditional weavers and carvers at work.
Another important cultural practice that is performed at the center is the haka, a traditional group dance.
It expresses the strength and unity of the Maori people, so be sure not to miss this!

sets.name: Unit 10 Reading 4 The Great Straw Debate
sents: Some people look at a straw and claim it has two holes, one at the top and one at the bottom.
But they’re misunderstanding what a “hole” actually is.
A hole isn’t defined by how many openings it has, but by the path it forms.
There are many examples to prove this.
Think of a doughnut: there’s a single circular hole in the center, not two.
The straw works the same way.
The hollow inside is one unbroken tunnel that connects both ends, and that tunnel is the hole.
Also, if you poke a pencil through a piece of paper, you make one hole, even if it shows on both sides.
Therefore, a straw features just one continuous hole.
A straw has two holes, one at each end.
Being connected doesn’t mean they’re the same.
Think about real-world usage.
If you asked someone to cover “the hole” in a straw, they’d have to ask, “Which one?”
That’s because each end functions independently.
A hallway with a door at each end still has two openings, and so does a tunnel.
We acknowledge both ends because each one gives access in its own right.
If one end gets blocked, the other is still there—it doesn’t vanish.
